headline.en: Sakura Sakura: hear the whole song first, then the tune on its own.

detail.en: The whole song, every part together
The guide sings it, line by line
Stop if anything tightens or hurts

headline.en: Now the tune on its own.

detail.en: Follow the words as it plays

text.en: Find the notes of line 1: each one waits until you're on it.
This song was first printed in 1888 by Tokyo's music school in a collection of music for the koto, a long zither, with the tune written in Western notes.

source.en: Sōkyokushū (Ministry of Education, Tokyo, 1888), No. 2, read from the scan

text.en: Hear line 1, then sing it back.
Hear line 2, then sing it back.
Now lines 1 and 2 joined: hear them, then sing them back.
Hear line 3, then sing it back.
Line 4 is the tune of line 2 again, with new words. Sing it with the guide.
Line 5 is the tune of line 3 again, with new words. Sing it with the guide.
Now lines 3 to 5 joined: hear them, then sing them back.
Hear line 6, then sing it back.
Hear line 7, then sing it back.
Now lines 6 and 7 joined: hear them, then sing them back.
The whole song, with the guide.
Sing your part with the other parts, and the guide with you. Hold your line while the others move.
The guide drops out: your part with the others only. Give me my note plays your first note quietly.
Once more on your own, from the top.
Record the tune of Sakura Sakura in Sing, with the other parts playing.
The tune uses only five notes, the in scale of Japanese koto music, and ends on a note that sounds open rather than finished.
